extracted.intended_audience: researchers, students, policymakers, and the general public seeking country-level demographic, military, and maritime data
extracted.subtask_description: A country-by-country reference listing specific metrics (literacy rates with definitions, military manpower estimates for ages 15-49, and maritime claim types/limits) with years/notes. Used for lookup and comparative research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literacy — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: definition: age 15 and over can read and write (with country-specific variants such as 'has completed five or more years of schooling', 'has ever attended school', or 'NA').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists a per-country 'definition' field indicating how literacy is defined for that country (e.g., 'age 15 and over can read and write', 'has completed five or more years of schooling', 'has ever attended school', or 'NA'). Users should note that definitions vary by country and affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literacy — total population (%)
rubrics_metrics.description: total population: (percentage) — e.g., 'total population: 98.6%' or 'total population: 74.2%'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent literacy for the total population age 15+ provided per country, usually with an 'est.' year. Values are point estimates (often followed by year and 'est.') and should be treated as approximate for that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literacy — male (%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Male literacy rate (age 15+) given per country when available. Not all entries include male/female breakdowns (some show NA). Compare with female values carefully because definitions may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literacy — female (%)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Female literacy rate (age 15+) given per country when available. Many entries include an associated year (e.g., '2003 est.'); some entries lack gender splits or are NA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literacy — variant and missing-value notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Occurrences of special notes such as 'definition: NA', 'total population: NA', or alternative definitions ('has completed five or more years of schooling', 'has ever attended school').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset uses 'NA' and other shorthand for missing/unavailable data and records cases where the literacy definition deviates from standard 'can read and write'. Users should treat these as metadata about measurement differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military manpower — males age 15-49 (count)
rubrics_metrics.description: males age 15-49: (numeric count) — e.g., 'males age 15-49: 6,785,414 (2004 est.)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides estimated counts of males aged 15–49 per country (usually with '2004 est.'). This is the primary military-availability metric on the page and is given as an estimate for a specified year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military manpower — females age 15-49 (count)
rubrics_metrics.description: females age 15-49: (numeric count) — present for some countries (e.g., 'females age 15-49: 12,457,077 (2004 est.)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some country entries also report female counts for ages 15–49. Where present, they are shown alongside male counts; often only males are listed. Year labels ('est.') accompany counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military manpower — notes on inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasional notes such as 'note: includes non-nationals (2004 est.)' attached to a country's manpower figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some country estimates include non-nationals or have other caveats; users should inspect per-country notes for composition differences that affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime claims — territorial sea
rubrics_metrics.description: territorial sea: (distance in nm or 'none (landlocked)') — commonly '12 nm', but other values appear (e.g., 3 nm, 4 nm, 6 nm, 50 nm, 200 nm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The territorial sea distance is provided per country; typical claim is 12 nautical miles but exceptions exist. Landlocked countries are listed as 'none (landlocked)'. Specific local exceptions (e.g., varied limits in straits) are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime claims — contiguous zone
rubrics_metrics.description: contiguous zone: (distance in nm) — commonly '24 nm', with variations such as 10 nm, 18 nm, 41 nm or absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a contiguous zone is claimed, its breadth is noted. Many countries claim the standard 24 nm, but some list different distances; absence indicates no contiguous zone claimed or not specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime claims — exclusive economic zone (EEZ)
rubrics_metrics.description: exclusive economic zone: (distance in nm or qualifiers) — commonly '200 nm', sometimes limited by treaties or 'NA'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most countries list a 200 nm EEZ; exceptions, treaty-defined limits, or non-application in specific seas (e.g., Mediterranean) are noted. Some entries show 'NA' for unavailable data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime claims — continental shelf
rubrics_metrics.description: continental shelf: (distance/criterion) — e.g., '200 nm or to the edge of the continental margin', '200-m depth or to the depth of exploitation', '200/350 nm'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continental shelf claims vary: some countries claim 200 nm, others claim to the edge of the continental margin or to depths/limits of exploitation. Specific phrasing per country indicates the legal/technical basis of the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime claims — exclusive fishing zone / exclusive fishing rights
rubrics_metrics.description: exclusive fishing zone / exclusive fishing zone: (distance in nm) — e.g., 'exclusive fishing zone: 200 nm', 'exclusive fishing zone: 12 nm', 'exclusive fishing zone: 25 nm'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fishing-zone claims are listed separately when applicable and may differ from EEZ breadth. Some territories use 'exclusive fishing zone' instead of EEZ; entries specify values and treaty-based exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime claims — measurement base and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases like 'measured from claimed archipelagic baselines' and 'measured from claimed archipelagic straight baselines' or 'measured from the mean low-tide baseline'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page indicates the baseline from which maritime distances are measured for some entities (important for interpreting breadth). Users must account for baseline method (straight baselines, archipelagic baselines, mean low-tide baseline) when comparing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime claims — disputes, reservations, and special-status notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes about non-acceptance or dispute (e.g., Antarctic EEZ claims not accepted by other countries; 'Western Sahara contingent upon resolution of sovereignty issue'; 'Gaza Strip - status subject to interim agreement').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset annotates claims with dispute or recognition caveats. Users should treat some claims as contested or not universally recognized; the page sometimes references treaties or bilateral agreements affecting limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data vintage, estimate labels, and missing-data flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of year labels and qualifiers such as '(2003 est.)', '(2004 est.)', 'NA', and 'No data available'. Also 'This page was last updated on 10 February, 2005'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each numeric entry is typically followed by a year and 'est.' indicating an estimate; 'NA' and 'No data available' mark missing values. The page's last-update timestamp indicates overall currency; users must consider data vintage when using or comparing figures.
